Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 8 May 2029 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity choice & data-fencing — operational handoff and evidence request

Hi Chris / Maya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and a proposed operational handoff so your security and infra teams can validate the deployment path. High level we heard two preferences during the call:

- Primary: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) to meet predictable throughput and to keep data plane isolated from multiservice tenants.
- Fallback: Private VPC deployment if BrightCare requires customer-managed networking and on-prem control of the control plane.

Key asks from BrightCare that we noted:
1) No multi-tenant memory persistence of customer prompts (explicit KV cache isolation).
2) KMS integration or HSM for key custody at rest for model artifacts and logs.
3) Audit log retention and export (90 days min), with SSO/SAML integration for operator access.

Next steps I propose:
- Jordan: lead operational handoff and supply the isolation evidence checklist we discussed (attachment).
- Karthik: confirm the network diagram for Dedicated vs Private VPC options and list any service egress points.
- Chris/Maya: share target SLA (p95 latency) and expected concurrent sessions for sizing.

Please see the attached "isolation-evidence-checklist.pdf" for the items your security team can use for an initial review. I can loop in our solutions engineer if you want a short walkthrough of the checklist.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0198

Attachment: isolation-evidence-checklist.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@brightcare.health>

Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity choice & data-fencing — operational handoff and evidence request

Tessa —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side after sharing this with security and procurement:

- Isolation: We need assurance that KV cache never persists across customers and that memory is zeroed between model sessions. Is that covered under both Dedicated and Private VPC options, or only Private VPC?
- KMS: We prefer customer-managed keys. If Dedicated supports BYOK with a control-plane stub within our VPC, that would be ideal. Is BYOK supported for Dedicated?
- Audit/export: Procurement asked whether audit logs can be pushed to our Splunk endpoint (HTTPS) in near-real time.

Also attaching two items your team requested: estimated concurrency (see attached spreadsheet) and a short description of our compliance checklist. Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up with Jordan & Karthik tomorrow to go over the technical evidence?

Thanks,
Chris
Director of IT Security | BrightCare Health
Attachment: brightcare-concurrency-2029.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)

Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity choice & data-fencing — operational handoff and evidence request

Hi Chris —

Thanks for the notes and attachment. Quick answers inline below: 

- KV cache isolation: Both Dedicated and Private VPC support per-customer KV caches with strict tenant isolation. The difference is in network control and control plane residency: Dedicated keeps the control plane in our managed environment but isolates inference instances in reserved pools; Private VPC moves the control plane into your VPC (or on-prem) which gives you direct network-level control. Either option provides the memory-zero/ephemeral cache behavior you asked about.

- BYOK for Dedicated: We support customer-managed keys via a KMS integration for Dedicated deployments (you can bring keys from AWS KMS or an HSM). For Private VPC, BYOK is of course supported since the control plane is in your environment. I'll include our KMS integration docs in the hub link.

- Audit/log export: We can stream audit logs to your Splunk endpoint using secure HTTPS forwarders; near-real-time export is supported.

Proposed 30-min slot: Fri 10 May, 10:00–10:30 PT. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and attach a network diagram and a one-page ops handoff that maps each evidence item to who provides it.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
